interface.name: sway_session_lock_config_v1
interface.description:
This sway-specific protocol extension allows a session lock client to configure how the compositor handles the lock screen background.
By default, the compositor renders an opaque background color behind session lock surfaces to ensure that no unlocked content is visible, as required by the ext-session-lock-v1 specification. This interface allows the lock client to opt out of that opaque background after the session has been locked, enabling transparent or semi-transparent lock surfaces through which the desktop content is visible.
The security model is as follows: the opaque blanking background is always presented first when a lock is initiated. Only after the lock is established may the client request that the background become transparent. This ensures that unlocked content is never visible during the lock transition, only after the lock client has explicitly opted in to transparency.
This is a privileged interface.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroys the config object. This does not affect the transparency state of any active session lock.

request.name: set_background_transparent
request.description:
Sets whether the compositor should allow desktop content to be visible behind session lock surfaces.
When transparent is non-zero, the compositor will not draw an opaque background behind session lock surfaces, allowing desktop content to show through transparent regions of the lock surface.
When transparent is zero (the default), the compositor draws an opaque background to hide all unlocked content.
This request takes effect immediately if a session lock is active. If no session lock is currently active, the value is stored and will apply to the next session lock.

arg.name: transparent
arg.summary: non-zero to allow transparency, zero for opaque
